title: Measurement error, residuals and disturbances
summary: Observed indicators contain measurement error, endogenous constructs have disturbances, and ignoring error weakens the relationships you estimate.

body.text: No indicator measures its construct perfectly. In a reflective model each indicator is the construct plus an error: the [[measurement-error]] contains random noise and anything specific to that item.

body.explanation: Indicator xᵢ equals its loading λᵢ times the construct ξ plus an error εᵢ that is uncorrelated with ξ. With standardised variables, λᵢ² is the share of the indicator's variance due to the construct: its reliability.

body.text: An endogenous construct has a [[disturbance]] ζ: the combined effect of every cause not in the model. 1 − R² is the share of its variance left to the disturbance; an R² below 1 is expected, not a defect. More generally a [[residual]] is the difference between what is observed and what the model implies.

Error matters because random error weakens observed relationships. If two constructs correlate ρ, scores with reliabilities r_x and r_y correlate only about ρ·√(r_x·r_y). CB-SEM and consistent PLS model the error of common-factor constructs explicitly; classic PLS composites contain it (Dijkstra & Henseler 2015).

mistake.title: Treating scale scores as error-free
mistake.text: Averaging items and running a regression on the averages treats them as perfectly reliable, which attenuates the effects you estimate. Models that separate error from the construct, or at least a report of reliability, are needed to judge how much.

tryIt.task: Open the TAM example and run it. For each endogenous construct, compute 1 − R², the share of variance left to its disturbance.

checks.question: Two constructs correlate .60. Each is measured with reliability .80. What correlation do you expect between their observed scores?

options.feedback: That would require perfectly reliable scores. Random error always weakens the observed correlation.
Dividing by the reliability is the correction for attenuation, which goes from observed to true, not the other way.
That multiplies by .80 twice. The factor is the square root of the product of the two reliabilities, here .80.

checks.explanation: Attenuation: observed r ≈ true r × √(reliability_x × reliability_y).

checks.question: BI has R² = .33. What does the disturbance of BI represent?

options.text: All influences on BI that the model does not contain, about 67% of its variance here.
options.feedback: Correct. The disturbance collects omitted causes and randomness.

options.text: Measurement error in the BI items.
options.feedback: Item errors belong to the measurement model. The disturbance is a structural-level residual of the construct itself.

options.text: A sign that the model is wrong.
options.feedback: Almost every behavioural outcome has causes outside a given model. An R² below 1 is normal.

checks.explanation: Disturbance = the unexplained part of an endogenous construct.
